figures.finding: From 1 January 2025 a screen actor's pay may not fall below the entry fee of €1,100 a shooting day for the first five days on a production and €900 for each day after; the floor does not bind for actors under 18, drama students, untrained lay actors, high-frequency TV (over 16 programme minutes a day) or low-budget cinema (under €15,000 a minute). A working day counts at least 8 hours, the regular week is 40 hours, the daily cap 12.

figures.finding: Screen actors' union is the Bundesverband Schauspiel (BFFS): €180 a year up to €50,000 gross earnings, €320 to €90,000, €450 above, €50 for drama students, plus a €50 joining fee; the collective agreements bind only members of the signing parties (TVG §3). Membership is not a condition of being cast: no agreement or law sets one, the BFFS–ARD remuneration rules apply to actors whether or not they belong to the BFFS, and the screen-actor agreement counts BFFS membership as only one of several marks of a professional actor (training, three productions, a year on stage, a ZAV listing).
